newsitem.title: UK: HK stocks in London end higher on short covering.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks in London end higher on short covering.

text.p: Hong Kong shares in London ended higher on Tuesday on short covering and with property shares still dominating the buoyant market, dealers said.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index ended 78.29 points or 0.6 percent higher at 13,135.22, after the Hang Seng index in Hong Kong rose 0.1 percent.
"There is buying activity mainly in the property sector in the market today...possibly related to some short covering," one dealer said.
Dealers said the market did see much turnover in the banks, but added they believed Hong Kong shares would remain on their upward tack in coming days.
HSBC Holdings fell 40 HK cents in London from its Hong Kong close at HK$157.60, reflecting a decline in the sterling-denominated shares, after dropping HK$2.00 in Hong Kong.
